papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics of Ciona adult brains reveals functional zonalization and insights into neural gland function.
papers.abstract: The ascidian Ciona is a pivotal chordate model for illuminating the evolutionary origins of the vertebrate brain. Here, spatial transcriptomics of the adult Ciona neural complex, combined with image-based computational super-resolution mapping, resolved distinct tissue domains including the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, ciliated funnel, neural gland duct/dorsal strand, and body wall muscle. Within the cerebral ganglion, high-resolution mapping revealed clear molecular zonalization separating the cortex and medulla, alongside regional specialization within the cortex itself. The neural gland
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics and computational super-resolution mapping to the adult Ciona neural complex, resolving distinct tissue domains including the cerebral ganglion, neural gland, and associated structures. It reveals molecular zonalization within the cerebral ganglion, separating cortex and medulla with further regional specialization, and provides new insights into neural gland function. The work establishes Ciona as a useful model for understanding the evolutionary origins of vertebrate brain organization.

papers.title: Multi-modal analysis of vascular remodelling in human obliterative bronchiolitis after lung transplantation.
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is the leading cause of late morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation. Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS), a major CLAD phenotype, is characterized by obliterative bronchiolitis (OB). While microvascular perturbations are described in BOS, their cellular and molecular characteristics remain unclear. Intact human CLAD lungs (n=3) underwent hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) for three-dimensional vascular mapping. In OB-affected airways vs. controls (n=4 each), endothelial subtypes were characterized by multiplex immunofluores
papers.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
papers.summary: This study uses hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) and multiplex immunofluorescence to map vascular remodelling in human lungs with obliterative bronchiolitis (OB), a hallmark of chronic lung allograft dysfunction after transplantation. The authors identify distinct endothelial cell subtypes and microvascular changes in OB-affected airways compared to controls, providing a multi-modal cellular and molecular characterization of the vascular niche in this disease.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals atorvastatin modulates the tumor microenvironment to suppress breast cancer liver metastatic outgrowth.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains incurable, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological and preclinical evidence suggests statins suppress metastatic outgrowth, however the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We employed high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) to explore the cellular composition and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the metastatic microenvironment following atorvastatin treatment. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded breast cancer liver metastases from control and atorvastatin-treated mice were analyzed by Nanostring CosMx Spatial Molecul
papers.summary: Using high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Nanostring CosMx) on mouse breast cancer liver metastases, the authors show that atorvastatin alters the cellular composition and gene expression of the metastatic microenvironment. These changes are associated with suppression of metastatic outgrowth, suggesting statins may act partly through remodeling the tumor microenvironment rather than only on tumor cells.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: This paper proposes a per-edge arbitration approach for gene regulatory network inference, using a gradient-boosted meta-classifier trained on the raw scores from ten different inference methods (including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR, and ARACNe). Instead of choosing one method or averaging all methods, the classifier learns to weight each method differently for each candidate regulator-target edge, and the authors also develop a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: FAP+ pericyte-like cells promote monocyte differentiation into tumor-associated macrophages in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive primary brain tumor characterized by profound immunosuppression that facilitates tumor progression and promotes therapeutic resistance. Fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a recognized theranostic target in multiple cancers, is upregulated in GBM and predominantly expressed by pericyte-like stromal cells. Here we identify a role for FAP⁺ pericyte-like cells in shaping the GBM immune microenvironment through monocyte recruitment and differentiation. Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) datasets, supported by reverse-transcription quantitative PCR
papers.summary: This study identifies FAP-expressing pericyte-like stromal cells in glioblastoma as key drivers of immunosuppression, recruiting monocytes and promoting their differentiation into tumor-associated macrophages. Using TCGA data and experimental validation, the authors establish FAP+ pericytes as a mechanism linking the tumor stroma to the immunosuppressive myeloid compartment, highlighting FAP as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveal impaired metabolic liver zonation in acute-on-chronic liver failure.
papers.abstract: Extrahepatic organ failures are key determinants of acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF). While the role of systemic inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction in the pathogenesis of ACLF is well known, the contribution of the liver itself is less understood. We therefore performed transcriptome and functional analyses of the liver in order to identify hepatic drivers of ACLF.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map gene expression across liver zones in patients with acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF), revealing that the liver's normal metabolic zonation is disrupted. The findings suggest that impaired zonation within the liver itself contributes to the systemic organ failures characteristic of ACLF, beyond the known roles of inflammation and mitochondrial dysfunction.

papers.title: highSpaClone enables copy number alteration inference and tumor subclone analysis for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatially resolved transcriptomics (SRT) offers unprecedented opportunities to investigate tumor heterogeneity but poses substantial computational and analytical challenges. Here, we present highSpaClone, a computational framework for copy number alteration (CNA) inference and tumor subclone identification from high-resolution SRT data across multiple spatial scales. By integrating spatial constraints into CNA estimation and clonal clustering, highSpaClone enables neighboring spatial locations to share information, thereby improving the robustness of genomic signals and the acc
papers.summary: highSpaClone is a computational framework that infers copy number alterations and identifies tumor subclones from high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data. By incorporating spatial constraints into CNA estimation and clonal clustering, it allows neighboring spatial locations to share information, improving the robustness of genomic signals and subclone detection across multiple spatial scales.

papers.title: Polyethylene terephthalate micro-/nanoplastics suppress SAT1-dependent ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The potential association between micro-/nanoplastics and cancer has raised increasing concerns. However, research focusing specifically on breast cancer (BC), and particularly on triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), remains limited, leading to a critical gap in current knowledge. This study seeks to explore potential correlative effects of micro-/nanoplastic exposure on TNBC progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates how exposure to polyethylene terephthalate (PET) micro-/nanoplastics affects triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) progression. The authors find that these plastic particles suppress SAT1-dependent ferroptosis, a form of iron-dependent cell death, potentially promoting tumor survival. This suggests a novel mechanism linking environmental plastic pollution to cancer biology.

papers.title: Pan-cancer screening and integrative multi-omics and deep learning reveal the prognostic significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The prognostic relevance of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD)-colorectal cancer (CRC) shared host-microbe signatures in non-intestinal epithelial malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic and biological significance of an IBD-CRC shared host-microbe interactome signature in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA).
papers.summary: This study investigates whether a host-microbe interaction signature previously linked to inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer also has prognostic value in bladder urothelial carcinoma. Using pan-cancer screening combined with multi-omics integration and deep learning, the authors identify this shared signature as prognostically significant in BLCA.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Define Eosinophil Heterogeneity during Influenza A Virus-induced Exacerbation of Fungal Allergic Asthma in C57BL/6 mice.
papers.abstract: Although eosinophils are accepted as transcriptionally heterogeneous in asthma, how allergic inflammation shapes eosinophil states during influenza A virus (IAV) infection remains undefined. We integrated high-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, quantitative immunofluorescence imaging, and cell-cell communication analyses to profile murine lungs across naïve, asthma, influenza (Flu), and Asthma+Flu conditions. We identified three related eosinophil transcriptional states distributed along a disease-associated continuum. Eosinophils in the Flu-only condition preferen
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and imaging to map eosinophil heterogeneity in mouse lungs across naive, allergic asthma, influenza, and combined asthma+influenza conditions. It identifies three related eosinophil transcriptional states that shift along a disease-associated continuum, with influenza alone driving a distinct state preference. The work shows how viral infection reshapes eosinophil states during allergic airway inflammation.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from NSCLC patients to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) based on epithelial cell-derived genes, using machine learning to predict survival and immunotherapy response. Low-PIS patients showed better outcomes and higher immune infiltration, and ADAM12 was validated as a key functional regulator through cell line and mouse experiments. The work nominates ADAM12 and the PIS as potential biomarkers for stratifying NSCLC patients for immunotherapy.

papers.title: Adrenomedullin from spinal cord injury drives heterotopic ossification in skeletal muscle via a neuro-immune-bone axis.
papers.abstract: Neurological heterotopic ossification can rapidly arise in the periarticular muscles following spinal cord injury. However, the specific mechanism of how the injured central nervous system regulates heterotopic bone formation in peripheral tissues remains largely unexplored. Here we first demonstrate through single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic analysis that fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) contribute to heterotopic ossification in injured muscle tissues following spinal cord injury. Mechanistically, we define a neuro-immune-bone axis in which endothelial tip cells with
papers.summary: This study shows that spinal cord injury triggers heterotopic ossification (abnormal bone formation) in skeletal muscle through a neuro-immune-bone axis. Using single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, the authors identify fibroadipogenic progenitor cells (FAPs) as the key cell population driving this process, with adrenomedullin from injured spinal cord acting as a signal that links the nervous system to immune cells and bone formation.

papers.title: FABP4 characterizes metabolic-immune interactions and serves as a prognostic biomarker across gynecologic malignancies: a multi-omics integrative analysis.
papers.abstract: Gynecological malignancies-including breast, cervical, ovarian, endometrial cancers and uterine sarcoma-pose a serious threat to women's health owing to their high incidence, aggressiveness and frequent recurrence. Fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) is a key regulator of lipid metabolism and tumor metabolic reprogramming, yet systematic investigations of its role across gynecological malignancies remain scarce. Here, by integrating data from TCGA, GTEx and multiple public repositories, we performed a multi-omics, multi-scale analysis of five gynecological malignancies, encompassing transcrip
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data from TCGA, GTEx, and other public repositories to characterize the role of fatty acid-binding protein 4 (FABP4) across five gynecological malignancies. The authors find that FABP4 is linked to metabolic-immune interactions and propose it as a prognostic biomarker across these cancers. The work is largely a bioinformatics reanalysis of existing datasets rather than a new experimental or methodological advance.

papers.title: Cell-based therapies of autoimmune diseases in the context of artificial intelligence development.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are comprised of several chronic inflammatory conditions characterized by activation of autoreactive T and B lymphocytes and produces autoantibodies. While most of the current treatment options mainly rely on non-specific immunosuppression, stem cell based therapies can be a promising candidate for promoting "immune reset" and restore long term tolerance against these complex diseases. Stem cell based therapy eliminate autoreactive clones and reconstitute immune tolerance. Besides, mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs; also referred to as mesenchymal stem cells) have immunomodul
papers.summary: This review discusses how stem cell-based therapies, particularly hematopoietic stem cell transplantation and mesenchymal stromal cell treatments, can promote an 'immune reset' and restore long-term tolerance in autoimmune diseases by eliminating autoreactive immune clones. It also explores how artificial intelligence could be integrated into the development and optimization of these cell-based therapies.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten integrated machine learning algorithms to build an ac4C-related gene prognostic signature (acRGBS) for colon adenocarcinoma. The four-gene signature (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C) stratified patients by prognosis and was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features, with in vitro experiments validating TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: T cell-derived CCL5 drives macrophage immunometabolic remodeling in chronic prostatitis via the CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α axis.
papers.abstract: Chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CP/CPPS) affects millions of men, yet the immune circuits that sustain sterile prostatic inflammation and pain remain poorly defined. Here we identify a T cell-macrophage metabolic signaling axis that drives chronic prostatitis. Integrated analysis of mouse experimental autoimmune prostatitis, chronically inflamed human prostate tissue, single-cell transcriptomes and spatial profiles revealed a population of glycolytic, HIF-1α-activated inflammatory macrophages enriched in diseased prostate niches. T cell-derived CCL5 was markedly induced and s
papers.summary: This study identifies a T cell-macrophage signaling circuit that drives chronic prostatitis, where T cell-derived CCL5 activates macrophages through the CCR5-ERK-PKM2/HIF-1α axis, promoting glycolytic reprogramming and inflammation. Integrated mouse, human tissue, single-cell, and spatial analyses reveal a pathogenic population of HIF-1α-activated inflammatory macrophages enriched in diseased prostate niches.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a prognostic gene signature linked to tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The signature captures tumor growth kinetics and may reveal therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the immune microenvironment.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long reads. The authors generated paired short-read and long-read single-cell datasets to evaluate how well different bioinformatics methods detect isoforms and alternative splicing. The work provides guidance on tool selection for researchers working with long-read single-cell transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors, such as a third-order drug-response tensor combined with a second-order transcriptomics matrix. It combines group factor analysis and tensor decomposition to learn interpretable latent factors, enabling joint analysis of heterogeneous experimental designs that existing methods cannot handle.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: The authors present sPYce, a computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across species without requiring sequence alignment. This enables direct comparison of chromatin accessibility and regulatory programs between species, addressing a gap that existing single-cell gene expression integration methods handle poorly.

papers.title: High-Content CRISPR Screening: Methods and Applications.
papers.abstract: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-Cas9 screening has become a central technology in functional genomics, enabling genome-scale interrogation via pooled perturbations. Early CRISPR screens employed survival or simple phenotypic readouts to identify essential genes and drug resistance mechanisms. However, as biological questions have shifted toward understanding regulatory networks, cellular heterogeneity, and context-dependent gene functions, there has been increasing demand for screening strategies capable of capturing complex cellular phenotypes beyond cell fi
papers.summary: This review covers high-content CRISPR screening, an approach that combines CRISPR-based genetic perturbations with imaging or other rich phenotypic readouts to capture complex cellular phenotypes beyond simple survival. It discusses the methods and applications of these screens, which enable interrogation of regulatory networks, cellular heterogeneity, and context-dependent gene functions.

papers.title: Increased Amyloidogenic Neuronal Injury in HIV-1-infected APP-KI Alzheimer's disease mice.
papers.abstract: A higher incidence of dementia, including Alzheimer's-like pathology, is observed in aged people living with human immunodeficiency virus-1 (HIV-1). However, mechanisms linking HIV-1 to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology remain unclear, due to the lack of animal models that allow for concurrent studies of HIV-1 and AD.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: This study develops a mouse model combining HIV-1 infection with Alzheimer's disease-like amyloid pathology (APP-KI mice) to investigate how HIV-1 may accelerate or exacerbate AD-related neuronal injury. The authors report increased amyloidogenic neuronal damage in co-affected mice, suggesting HIV-1 infection can potentiate Alzheimer's-type pathology. This provides a new experimental platform for studying the intersection of HIV-1 and AD.

papers.title: Decoding cell-cell communication in spatial transcriptomics: mechanistic insights, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is essential for maintaining tissue organization and driving biological progression, yet its inference from transcriptomic data has long been limited by the absence of spatial context. Advances in spatial transcriptomics (ST) now enable mechanistically grounded analyses of CCC by preserving the physical organization of cells and their microenvironments. In this review, we examine recent methodological developments in CCC inference from ST data, focusing on how statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks incorporate spatial information to model lig
papers.summary: This review surveys recent computational methods for inferring cell-cell communication (CCC) from spatial transcriptomics data, covering statistical, optimal transport, and deep learning frameworks that leverage spatial context. It highlights mechanistic insights gained, modeling constraints, and analytical caveats that researchers should consider when interpreting CCC results.

papers.title: EGFR-Mutant Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer With Small Cell Transformation: Clinicopathological Features, Treatment Landscape, and Biomarker Profiles.
papers.abstract: Transformed small-cell lung cancer (tSCLC) is a clinically important resistance mechanism to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer. This study characterizes clinical features, treatment outcomes, and biomarker profiles in patients with tSCLC.
papers.summary: This study characterizes transformed small-cell lung cancer (tSCLC), a resistance mechanism that can emerge in EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer after tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. It describes the clinical and pathological features of these patients, their treatment outcomes, and associated biomarker profiles. The work aims to improve recognition and management of this aggressive transformation event.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing with machine learning to dissect the ovarian cancer microenvironment, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight residual fibroblast-enriched disease as a therapeutic vulnerability and demonstrate the utility of combining single-cell data with predictive modeling to stratify patients.

papers.title: Stage-specific ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis: predictive immune insights into the MIF pathway and HLA-DR/IL2RA axis via integrated GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial profiling.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence links reactive oxygen species modulator 1 (ROMO1), a key mitochondrial ROS regulator, to rheumatoid arthritis (RA) pathogenesis. However, its exact mechanism remains elusive given the conflicting evidence about its specific function. We used a four-level integrative framework combining multi-omics data and literature‑supported mechanistic inference. At the genetic level, Mendelian randomization (MR) was performed to explore potential causal relationships between ROMO1, IL2RA, HLA-DR, MIF, and RA risk, followed by differential expression analysis and machine learning-based fea
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial data to investigate the role of ROMO1 in rheumatoid arthritis, finding stage-specific expression patterns and links to the MIF pathway and an HLA-DR/IL2RA immune axis. The authors propose ROMO1 as a potential predictive biomarker and mechanistic contributor to RA pathogenesis.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the gene RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify Bregs and RPS2 as potential drivers of metastasis, suggesting they could serve as therapeutic targets to prevent bone metastasis in NPC patients.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and treatment resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and the formation of immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis. The findings point to STC1 as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target warranting further study.

papers.title: Microplastics and nanoplastics-related genes signature predicts prognosis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and functional validation of interleukin 1 alpha.
papers.abstract: Microplastics and nanoplastics (MNPs), as emerging environmental pollutants, have garnered significant attention from the global scientific community due to their potential threats to human health, particularly their association with the occurrence and development of cancer. The goal of our study is to create a predictive marker for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PAAD) based on MNPs-related genes, with the purposes of predicting survival outcomes and assessing the tumor immune microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study builds a prognostic gene signature for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma based on genes associated with microplastic and nanoplastic exposure, and validates interleukin 1 alpha as a functionally relevant gene. The signature is intended to predict patient survival and characterize the tumor immune microenvironment. It represents an early attempt to link environmental pollutant exposure to cancer prognosis through transcriptomic modeling.

papers.title: RECQL correlates with immune infiltration and serves as a prognostic biomarker and therapeutic predictor in gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: RecQ-like helicase (RECQL), a member of the RecQ-like DNA helicase family, plays a crucial role in maintaining genomic stability. However, its relevance in gastric cancer (GC) has not been fully investigated. This study aimed to explore the clinical significance, biological functions, and potential role of RECQL in the tumor immune microenvironment of GC through comprehensive bioinformatics analyses and in vitro experiments.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of RECQL, a DNA helicase involved in genomic stability, in gastric cancer using bioinformatics and in vitro experiments. The authors find that RECQL expression correlates with immune cell infiltration and may serve as a prognostic biomarker and predictor of therapeutic response in gastric cancer patients.

papers.title: Multi-omics characterization of a GPRC5A+ epithelial subpopulation associated with malignant features in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits marked cellular heterogeneity, and the cellular context of malignancy-associated epithelial programs remains incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify and characterize a GPRC5A+ epithelial subpopulation in colorectal cancer that is linked to malignant features. The authors show that this subpopulation exhibits distinct molecular characteristics associated with tumor aggressiveness, providing a more detailed view of CRC cellular heterogeneity.

papers.title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders (DD) are highly heterogeneous psychiatric illnesses. Their complex pathogenesis, coupled with suboptimal response rates to current clinical treatments, poses significant challenges to global mental health. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of DD at the transcriptomic level. This paper reviews recent advances utilizing bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), and single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) to explore the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), perinatal depression (PND), per
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent applications of bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing to study the molecular pathogenesis of depressive disorders, including major depressive disorder and perinatal depression. It highlights how transcriptomic approaches are revealing cellular and molecular heterogeneity underlying these conditions while also discussing remaining technical and interpretive challenges.

papers.title: Single-cell Raman profiling of B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation with transcriptome inference.
papers.abstract: Label-free profiling of cellular transcriptional and metabolic states during B cell differentiation and malignant transformation remains technically challenging. Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive alternative for single-cell biochemical characterization, yet its ability to infer transcriptomic profiles and distinguish leukemic cells has been limited.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell Raman spectroscopy to profile B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation, aiming to infer transcriptomic states from label-free biochemical signatures. The work suggests Raman profiling can distinguish leukemic cells from normal differentiating B cells without destructive labeling.

papers.title: From transcriptomic profiling to precision oncology: a bibliometric analysis of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become an important tool for investigating the molecular heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); however, the global development and thematic evolution of this field remain inadequately characterized.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia, examining publication trends, key contributors, and thematic evolution over time. It aims to characterize how transcriptomic profiling has progressed toward precision oncology applications in AML, though the abstract provides limited detail on specific findings.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates peripheral blood cell patterns in patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy. By combining pharmacovigilance data with single-cell analysis, the authors aim to identify early markers of severe (fulminant) cases and characterize the immune cell changes in the blood that underlie this condition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived lung model that contains multiple epithelial lineages with both proximal and distal features, overcoming the single-lineage limitation of prior organoid systems. This multi-lineage model can be used to study idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis mechanisms and screen potential drugs in a more physiologically relevant context.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific macrophage population marked by JAML expression and lipid-associated gene programs. Using transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS), single-cell profiling, and spatial fibrotic niche analysis, the authors identify this JAML+ macrophage program as a key mediator linking genetic susceptibility to peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Machine learning approaches were used to prioritize this cell state as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics and a boundary wound model reveal temporal decoupling and microenvironmental heterogeneity in radiation-induced fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a key treatment method for cancer, but high-dose treatment can lead to damage to normal tissues and chronic fibrosis. There is a lack of systematic temporal analysis of the dynamic progression from early damage signals to late extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell transcriptomics combined with a boundary wound model to track how radiation-induced fibrosis develops over time. The authors find that early damage signaling and later extracellular matrix deposition are temporally decoupled, and that the fibrotic microenvironment is heterogeneous across different cell populations. This provides a more systematic temporal map of the transition from acute radiation damage to chronic fibrosis.

papers.title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA.
papers.abstract: Gene expression profiling of single cells using single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sxRNA-seq) enables researchers to characterize cellular heterogeneity and unraveling complex biological processes at unprecedented resolution. However, sxRNA-seq faces challenges due to the presence of ambient RNA, extraneous RNA molecules not originating from the cells of interest. Sample preparation is a major source of ambient RNA, where harsh conditions can lead to cell lysis and the release of intracellular RNA. This inescapable inclusion of ambient RNA can cause erroneous results and hinder dow
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for removing ambient RNA contamination from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. Ambient RNA, released from lysed cells during sample preparation, can distort gene expression profiles and lead to false biological conclusions. The study systematically compares available decontamination tools to guide researchers in choosing appropriate approaches.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of MBNL2 associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) improves outcomes in resectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), yet response varies widely and current biomarkers lack precision. Novel correlates of immunotherapy sensitivity tailored to the LUSC tumor microenvironment (TME) are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics profiling to identify MBNL2 as a molecular feature associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma. The finding suggests MBNL2 could serve as a candidate biomarker for stratifying patients who are less likely to benefit from this treatment approach.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures associated with prognosis and immune landscape. Using the AUCell algorithm, the authors identified 630 lactylation-associated genes and developed a prognostic signature linking lactylation activity to tumor microenvironment and immune cell infiltration. The findings suggest lactylation may serve as a biomarker and therapeutic target in cervical cancer.

papers.title: Spatial immune dysregulation in MASLD: integration of lobular zoning, metabolism and immune function.
papers.abstract: Most prior studies on immune-related fatty liver disease have focused on changes in immune cell quantity and composition. However, this "cell-count model" does not fully explain the regional onset of fibrosis, spatial heterogeneity of lesions, or variable immunotherapy responses. Immune dysregulation in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) involves not only compositional changes but also spatial redistribution and functional alterations of immune cells within specific hepatic lobule regions. Emerging multi-omics and spatial transcriptomic data suggest that chemokine
papers.summary: This review argues that immune dysregulation in MASLD is not just about changes in immune cell numbers, but also involves spatial redistribution and functional changes of immune cells within specific hepatic lobule zones. It highlights how emerging multi-omics and spatial transcriptomics data link lobular zoning, metabolism, and immune function to better explain regional fibrosis onset and variable immunotherapy responses.

papers.title: Spatial dynamics of cancer-associated fibroblasts links fibroblastic differentiation to immune exclusion and tumor progression.
papers.abstract: Although the role of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) in cancer progression is increasingly recognized, their spatial dynamics and interactions with immune cells remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study examines the spatial organization of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) within tumors and how their differentiation states relate to immune cell exclusion and tumor progression. The authors link specific fibroblastic differentiation programs to the spatial exclusion of immune cells, suggesting CAFs actively shape an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Case Report: Post-mortem analysis of long-term inflammation after mild COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Persistent inflammation and tissue injury may contribute to post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). However, direct tissue evidence from mildly-infected individuals sampled long after recovery remains exceptionally limited. Here, we performed post-mortem bulk RNA-seq and GeoMx digital spatial profiling of lung, heart, and brain tissues from four individuals who recovered from mild COVID-19 more than 250 days before death from unrelated causes. Samples were collected during the early phase of the national vaccination program, before widespread vaccine uptake and recurrent infection, providing a ra
papers.summary: This case report performed post-mortem RNA-seq and spatial profiling on lung, heart, and brain tissues from four individuals who had recovered from mild COVID-19 more than 250 days before dying of unrelated causes. The authors found evidence of persistent inflammation and tissue injury long after recovery, suggesting a possible tissue-level basis for post-acute COVID-19 syndrome (PACS). The small sample size and case-report design limit generalizability.

papers.title: The PROM1+SMAD5+ Tumor-Initiating Subpopulation Shapes Premetastatic Niches through Spatial Multi-Omics Landscapes in HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer exhibits high metastatic potential, linked not only to intrinsic cancer cell traits but also to critical crosstalk with the tumor microenvironment. However, the coevolutionary mechanisms between cancer cells and multiple stromal subpopulations in driving distant metastasis remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the microenvironmental regulatory mechanisms of breast tumor-initiating cells and their roles in HER2-positive breast cancer metastasis. Methods: Integrated multi-omics analyses
papers.summary: This study uses integrated spatial multi-omics to characterize a PROM1+SMAD5+ tumor-initiating subpopulation in HER2-positive breast cancer and shows how these cells interact with stromal populations to shape premetastatic niches. The findings link specific cancer cell states to microenvironmental remodeling that promotes distant metastasis, offering potential targets for intervention.

papers.title: OLR1 as a Key Inflammatory Regulator Associated with Poor Response to Neoadjuvant Immunochemotherapy in Resectable Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy (nICT) limits long-term survival in resectable lung cancer. How to improve response rates and the regulatory mechanism of tumor inflammatory signaling in nICT efficacy remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study identifies OLR1 (the oxidized LDL receptor 1) as a key inflammatory regulator whose expression is associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy in resectable lung cancer. The findings suggest OLR1 may serve as a biomarker for predicting treatment response and a potential target for improving nICT efficacy.

papers.title: Association Between Mutation Context-Associated RUNX1 Transcriptional States and Immune-Stromal Heterogeneity in Nonsmall Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: Nonsmall cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by substantial heterogeneity in driver mutation backgrounds and tumor microenvironment (TME) phenotypes, yet the transcriptional regulatory states linking genotype context to immune-stromal variation remain incompletely defined. In this study, we integrated mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA-LUAD/LUSC to construct a mutation-expression-matched NSCLC cohort and evaluated RUNX1 as a mutation context-associated transcriptional/regulatory state rather than as a recurrently mutated driver. Driver contexts were assessed using a pr
papers.summary: This study integrates mutation, transcriptomic, and clinical data from TCGA lung adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma cohorts to examine RUNX1 as a transcriptional regulatory state linked to specific driver mutation contexts rather than as a mutated driver gene itself. The authors find that mutation context-associated RUNX1 states correlate with immune-stromal heterogeneity in the tumor microenvironment, suggesting genotype context shapes regulatory programs influencing immune infiltration.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification and functional validation of signal regulatory protein gamma as a prognostic biomarker and immune regulator in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) comprises biologically diverse tumors, and durable responses to immune-checkpoint blockade are achieved by only a subset of patients. There remains a need for markers that connect clinical outcome with malignant-cell phenotypes and tissue-level immune organization.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics data to identify signal regulatory protein gamma (SIRPG) as a prognostic biomarker in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, linking its expression to patient outcomes and immune regulation. Functional validation experiments support SIRPG's role in modulating the tumor immune microenvironment, suggesting it could help stratify patients for immune-checkpoint blockade therapy.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal SERPINE1 as a Key Link Between Macro_SPP1 Macrophages and Stromal Remodeling in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Macrophage heterogeneity is increasingly recognized as an important feature of the gastric cancer tumor microenvironment, yet the macrophage states linked to poor outcome and the molecules connecting them to stromal remodeling remain incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing data from GSE183904, spatial transcriptomic data from GSE251950, and TCGA-STAD bulk transcriptomic data to characterize macrophage diversity and identify clinically relevant macrophage-associated genes. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed intensified intercellular signaling in tumors, with
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, and bulk TCGA data to characterize macrophage heterogeneity in gastric cancer, identifying a Macro_SPP1 macrophage population associated with poor outcomes. The authors highlight SERPINE1 as a key mediator linking these macrophages to stromal remodeling, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.
